description: Hand-labelled precision/recall set for the answer-credit check in CorrectnessReward: given a question, a short reference answer and a model reply, decide whether the reply commits to the reference as its single answer. Written blind to the implementation, from the kinds of replies real models and users produce. Labelling rule: 'credit' when the reply commits to the reference as its one answer; qualifiers, explanations, units, markdown, LaTeX/GSM8K-style final-answer markers, restating the question, intermediate arithmetic, and other entities mentioned as context (not as alternative answers) are fine, and so is rejecting a wrong option while committing to the reference (negation_correct). 'no_credit' when the reply hedges between the reference and any other candidate in any form (separators such as or/vs/&/+/->/em dash/colon/~/x/slash/pipe/semicolon, concessive 'though/although/some say', numeric conditionals such as '42; 43 if you round up', modal 'maybe X, maybe Y', or a list of candidates), gives a wrong answer, negates the reference, refuses, or gives no answer. Every hedge reply is labelled once with each candidate as the reference, and negation replies are mirrored with the rejected option as the reference, so a hedge or negation earns nothing whichever candidate is correct; those mirrored references are deliberately not always factually true. Replies whose only issue is admitted uncertainty about a single answer, and genuinely ambiguous replies, are excluded. Splits alternate dev/heldout within each category, with all items sharing the same question and reply kept in the same split.
